ch11_p9_chk1_solo.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk1_solo.mp3.text: Active Checkpoint 1: In a binary classification task with five independent workers, what is the exact majority vote accuracy when individual worker competence is eighty percent, versus when it drops to forty percent? Select Option A, B, C, or D above me!

ch11_p9_chk1_duo.mp3.speaker: Kaito
ch11_p9_chk1_duo.mp3.text: Checkpoint 1 time! Let's compute the binomial expansion for five annotators at eighty percent versus forty percent competence. Choose Option A, B, C, or D above me!

ch11_p9_chk1_feedback_correct.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk1_feedback_correct.mp3.text: Outstanding mathematical derivation! Option B is correct. For p equals zero point eight zero, the binomial sum over three, four, and five votes yields ninety-four point two one percent consensus accuracy. For p equals zero point four zero, consensus accuracy collapses down to thirty-one point seven four percent!

ch11_p9_chk1_feedback_incorrect.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk1_feedback_incorrect.mp3.text: Not quite. Option B is correct. Remember the Condorcet Jury Theorem: when competence is eighty percent, majority voting boosts accuracy to ninety-four point two one percent. But when competence is sub-chance at forty percent, majority voting amplifies error, dropping accuracy to thirty-one point seven four percent!

ch11_p9_chk2_solo.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk2_solo.mp3.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Three annotators evaluate a binary item: an expert with ninety-five percent sensitivity emits label one, while two noisy workers with sixty and fifty-five percent accuracy emit label zero. What is the exact Dawid-Skene posterior probability for class one? Choose Option A, B, C, or D above me!

ch11_p9_chk2_duo.mp3.speaker: Kaito
ch11_p9_chk2_duo.mp3.text: Checkpoint 2! Two crowd workers vote zero, but one top expert votes one. What does the Bayesian likelihood ratio compute for the true posterior? Select Option A, B, C, or D above me!

ch11_p9_chk2_feedback_correct.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk2_feedback_correct.mp3.text: Spot on Bayesian mastery! Option B is correct. The likelihood ratio for the expert is nineteen point zero, while the combined crowd likelihood ratio favoring class zero is only one point eight three. The resulting posterior probability for class one is ninety-one point two percent, overriding the two-to-one majority!

ch11_p9_chk2_feedback_incorrect.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk2_feedback_incorrect.mp3.text: Incorrect. Option B is correct. Simple majority assigns class zero, but Dawid-Skene weights evidence by observer confusion rates. The expert's nineteen-to-one likelihood ratio overwhelms the weak crowd votes, yielding ninety-one point two percent certainty for class one!

ch11_p9_chk3_solo.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk3_solo.mp3.text: Active Checkpoint 3: An enterprise legal discovery team faces budget exhaustion with crowd labelers stalling at seventy-nine percent recall. ch11_p9_chk3_duo.mp3.speaker: Kaito
ch11_p9_chk3_duo.mp3.text: Final checkpoint! How do we stop budget waste and cognitive fatigue in a high-stakes annotation pipeline? Choose Option A, B, C, or D above me!

ch11_p9_chk3_feedback_correct.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk3_feedback_correct.mp3.text: Brilliant operational diagnosis! Option B is correct. Deploying Dawid-Skene latent modeling on Tier 1 crowd workers, setting an entropy escalation threshold tau of zero point four zero for specialist review, and injecting ten percent synthetic gold honeypots simultaneously optimizes budget and accuracy!

ch11_p9_chk3_feedback_incorrect.mp3.speaker: Dr. Nova
ch11_p9_chk3_feedback_incorrect.mp3.text: Not quite. Option B is correct. Increasing crowd redundancy alone suffers from Sheng's diminishing returns of one over square root of K, while one hundred percent expert review is cost-prohibitive. The optimal solution combines Dawid-Skene crowd aggregation with entropy-based expert escalation!
